L168: ## Description
L169: ## Summary
L170: 
L171: Metalama loaded and executed compile-time assemblies, auxiliary executable tools, and embedded helper assemblies from predictable temporary directories. On Linux and macOS the default cache location was the world-writable system temporary directory (`Path.GetTempPath()`, i.e. `/tmp`), and previously-generated artifacts were trusted based on the presence of a sentinel/`.completed` marker file rather than on any integrity verification.
L172: A local, unprivileged user on a shared machine or CI/build agent can pre-create the deterministic cache directory structure and plant a malicious DLL together with the matching sentinel file. When a higher-privileged user (or build/service account) subsequently runs a build, Metalama finds the sentinel, skips regeneration, and loads and executes the attacker-supplied assembly inside the compiler / IDE / MSBuild process.
L173: 
L174: Affected load-and-execute paths:
L175:   * the cache of compile-time assemblies that Metalama generates from your aspects;
L176:   * auxiliary executable tools that Metalama extracts to a local directory and then launches;
L177:   * embedded .NET helper assemblies that Metalama extracts to a local directory and loads into the build / IDE process.
L178: ## Impact
L179: 
L180: Arbitrary code execution in the security context of the building user — i.e. a local privilege escalation across user accounts on shared POSIX systems (multi-user developer machines, CI/build agents). The attacker obtains code execution as the victim without holding the victim's privileges, and can read source/secrets, tamper with build output (supply-chain injection), or disrupt builds.
L181: ## Affected configurations
L182:   * Linux and macOS, default configuration — affected. The shipped default uses the world-writable system temp directory.
L183:   * Windows, default configuration — not affected. The default per-user temporary directory is protected by OS ACLs, so cross-user planting is not possible.
L184:   * The `METALAMA_TEMP` environment variable is a deployer-controlled override and is out of scope: pointing it at an insecure (e.g. world-writable or attacker-owned) location is a deployment misconfiguration, not a defect in the product.
L185: ## Severity
L186: 
L187: CVSS v3.1: `AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` = 8.2 (High) for the affected POSIX default configuration (Scope:Changed reflects the cross-user privilege escalation).
L188: 
L189: CVSS v4.0 cross-check: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:L/VI:H/VA:L/SC:L/SI:H/SA:H` = 6.0 (Medium), which more granularly attributes low impact to the cache itself and high impact to the subsequent build process. The honest range is therefore Medium-High depending on the scoring model and platform.
L190: ## Fix
L191: 
L192: Caches and extraction directories were relocated from the world-writable system temp directory to per-user application-data locations (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` / `~/.cache/Metalama` on POSIX), relying on OS-enforced per-user ownership as the trust boundary. Fixed in 2026.1.19.
L193:
